extracted.intended_audience: student affairs personnel and campus grant-writing teams in higher education
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for developing, writing, submitting, and managing external grant proposals originating from student affairs units at colleges/universities. Emphasizes team-based proposal development, RFP alignment, evaluation design, budgeting, submission, and post-award management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fit with institutional strategic plan and sponsor goals
rubrics_metrics.description: To receive funding, a proposal must demonstrate fit between the institutional strategic plan, the goals of the sponsor, and the objectives of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The strongest proposals demonstrate a rigorous alignment with guidelines of the sponsor. Even an idea with merit will not be funded if program goals do not align. Critically examine sponsors that possibly align with project idea and institution; many sponsors post past awardees to help assess fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify sponsors and research prior awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify funding sources (federal, state, private foundations, professional organizations) and research potential sponsors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for past awardees (institution, project, contacts). Campuses may use national search agencies to locate sponsors. Decide whether to submit to one or multiple agencies (if accepted by more than one, choose one and decline others).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assemble a representative writing team
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish a writing team that is representative of the project stakeholders and includes personnel familiar with the institutions or departments involved who have authority to commit resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designate a team leader (pre-determined or chosen). Team members must read the RFP carefully to identify required components. Include effective writers who can write to RFP parameters and complete assigned tasks timely. Leader facilitates focus on RFP requirements and maintains accountability and communication across the organizational flowchart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read and follow the RFP precisely
rubrics_metrics.description: Carefully read the RFP to identify requisite components, operational definitions, formatting rules, partner requirements, eligible/ineligible activities, and submission instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RFPs may specify font, page length, required partners, allowed activities, and submission methods. Failure to follow formatting and RFP instructions can result in rejection before review.

rubrics_metrics.name: General effective grant writing standards (outline and drafting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a thorough outline before writing that includes each section (in order) specified in the RFP; include as much information as possible in the first draft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An outline ensures completeness. First drafts should be substantive to avoid missing required information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing style and language choices
rubrics_metrics.description: Write with language that engages readers’ interest and employ the same language that is contained in the sponsor’s RFP; explain technical terms and use active voice where possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mirroring sponsor language helps reviewers see alignment. Clear, engaging prose aids comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make alignment/fit obvious early
rubrics_metrics.description: Make it very obvious early in the proposal that your project matches the interest of the funding agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staffs of funding sources say lack of a clear fit with priorities is the single most common reason for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer essential project questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Answer essential questions regarding what the project will accomplish, how it will do so, and what evidence will demonstrate that the goals have been accomplished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals must clearly state activities and the measurable evidence of success; link activities to objectives and goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logical, linear presentation tying goals→objectives→activities→outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow a logical and linear presentation: organize goals, objectives, activities, and outcomes so each activity has a measurable outcome and is linked to a specific objective linked to a specific goal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A good proposal will have only one or two overarching goals. Ensure each activity maps to measurable outcomes and objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present a strong evaluation design
rubrics_metrics.description: Present an evaluation design that generates the data needed to show the project has been successful; evaluation is essential to both the budget and the timeline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weak evaluation sections are a common basis for rejection. Ensure evaluation provides formative and summative assessments and connects to budget/time allocations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay close attention to formatting and administrative instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow instructions on page limitations, font size, margins, spacing, submission methods, deadlines, numbers of copies, and appendices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative noncompliance can result in a proposal being rejected before review. Check sponsor-specific formatting and submission requirements carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use campus resources for pre- and post-award functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage Offices of Sponsored Programs/Research, Development, Business Affairs, or Institutional Effectiveness/Research for assistance identifying funding, technical assistance, assembling teams, and grant management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These offices can help identify funding, provide data, assist with budget development, and guide submission and post-award administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use institutional data and needs assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Include needs assessment using relevant quantitative and qualitative data (institutional longitudinal data, demographics, economic/community/educational data) to justify the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offices of Institutional Effectiveness/Research often collect data useful for justification. RFPs may require specific types of data to support need and anticipated impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include appropriate partners and collaborations
rubrics_metrics.description: Include internal and/or external partners as required or to increase project impact; partners may be community agencies, local schools, faculty, counseling/students services, law enforcement, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some RFPs mandate external partners; others encourage cross-disciplinary collaboration. Identify partners and document their roles and commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow standard proposal component structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals typically include a summary, abstract, table of contents, introduction of the organization, problem statement/needs assessment, goals/objectives, management plan, evaluation plan, budget and budget narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsors provide grant writing guides; the RFP provides the outline the writing team must follow. Section titles may differ by sponsor but the core components remain similar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget drives objectives and demonstrates ethical/resource-appropriate planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing should begin with the end in mind: develop the budget early because RFPs specify allowable expenditures; the budget should communicate effective planning, ethical and appropriate use of funds, and allocation of resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The budget provides a foundation for program goals, timeline, personnel, and evaluation. Consider which elements are critical and which could be reduced if the sponsor negotiates budget reductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include a budget narrative and align expenditures to objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a budget narrative that explains all proposed expenditures and ensure budget follows campus fiscal policies and sponsor rules regarding allowable costs and matching requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offices of Sponsored Research and Business Affairs can assist. Identify matching resource expectations and comply with institutional procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop SMART objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Write effective objectives that follow the acronym SMART: sensible, measurable, attainable, realistic, and time-bound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objectives should communicate what the project will do, by when, by whom, and to what extent. Use the RFP priorities to derive goals and objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan timelines and allow time for collecting documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Factor sufficient time to collect necessary data, letters of support, and other documentation specified by the RFP and campus administrative processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants can take from a week to a year to prepare depending on sponsor timelines. Allow time for approvals and submission logistics (including electronic submission delays).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation plan: include formative and summative components and follow a clear template
rubrics_metrics.description: Design an evaluation that, at minimum, evaluates and modifies methods during the program (formative evaluation) and states criteria for success (summative evaluation). Follow steps: what to evaluate; what information is needed and how to collect it; how to analyze and report data; what resources are needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine audiences for evaluation, identify questions, performance targets, populations/data sources, methodologies, clearances/permissions (e.g., IRB), data collection timelines, analysis methods, reporting timelines, and budget for evaluation. Consider external evaluators if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include research component when required (literature review, hypotheses, design)
rubrics_metrics.description: If RFP requires a research component, submit a literature review, hypotheses, and an overview of research design complying with sponsor parameters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain current state of knowledge to show why the proposal is unique and significant. Ensure research methods (qualitative/quantitative) match sponsor expectations and/or document institutional experience conducting similar research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human subjects protections and IRB clearance
rubrics_metrics.description: If evaluation involves collecting data from human subjects, obtain Institutional Review Board (IRB) authorization prior to data collection and include docket numbers if required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsors may require IRB authorization as part of negotiation; campus must ensure ethical standards. Sponsors can audit compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission authority and required institutional signatures/forms
rubrics_metrics.description: A writing team cannot submit proposals on behalf of the institution without authorized institutional signatures; proposals often require application cover page, assurances, and specific budget forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain signature of the authorized official who can commit the campus to contracts and any additional signatures required by campus Offices of Sponsored Programs or Business Affairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic submission technical requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow sponsor electronic submission formats, which may require dividing proposals into sections, have file size limitations, and may be subject to server delays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow time for server issues on due dates and verify file formats and size limits; understand differences across sponsors' online systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-award negotiation and scope/budget adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: If funded, sponsors may negotiate the budget and the institution may negotiate reductions in scope if funding is reduced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop budgets that identify critical elements and enhancements that can be reduced if necessary. Manage grants according to campus policies and sponsor guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use reviewer feedback after declination
rubrics_metrics.description: If proposal is rejected, request reviewer comments (if not provided automatically) and use them to rework and resubmit to the next cycle or different sponsor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Private foundations seldom provide reviewer comments automatically; requesting feedback can help improve future submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate anticipated campus impact and alignment with institutional strengths/weaknesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Articulate how the project will affect campus departments and how it addresses institutional strengths and weaknesses relevant to the sponsor’s priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RFPs often require describing impact (e.g., Strengthening Institutions Program requires assessing fiscal stability, academic programs, institutional management). Use this analysis to develop goals/objectives that support the institutional strategic plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan for grant management and accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure project director and personnel manage the grant through campus policies and sponsor guidelines with clear communication, management plans, timelines, and evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective post-award management is facilitated by thorough communication during proposal development, a detailed budget, and clear management and timeline plans. Sponsors may audit compliance; maintain documentation.
